title: EXACT Commands to Create Everything
text:
This file contains the exact step-by-step commands to create the full prototype with PDF + Excel support and all 9 sample files.



cd /home/karthikean.juttumaha/mini-extract/prototype




Single command:
pip install openpyxl PyPDF2 pdfplumber reportlab python-magic 2>&1 | grep -v "already satisfied" || true
Individual installation (if above fails):
pip install openpyxl
pip install PyPDF2
pip install pdfplumber
pip install reportlab
pip install python-magic




mkdir -p samples results




Command:
python3 -c "
import re
with open('EXTRACTION_SCRIPT_FULL.md', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()
code = re.search(r'```python(.*?)```', content, re.DOTALL)
if code:
    with open('extract.py', 'w') as f:
        f.write(code.group(1))
    print('SUCCESS: extract.py created')
else:
    print('ERROR: Python code not found')
"
Verify:
ls -lh extract.py
head -5 extract.py




RUN THIS SINGLE COMMAND (RECOMMENDED):
cd /home/karthikean.juttumaha/mini-extract/prototype && (
# Text 1
cat > samples/text1.txt << 'EOF'
<!-- EDIT: 2024-01-01T10:00:00Z | AUTHOR: alice | TYPE: create -->
# Quarterly Report
Project Status: Active
Budget: $100,000

<!-- EDIT: 2024-01-02T14:30:00Z | AUTHOR: bob | TYPE: add -->
## Phase 1 Complete
All milestones achieved.

<!-- EDIT: 2024-01-03T09:15:00Z | AUTHOR: alice | TYPE: modify -->
## Phase 1 Complete
All milestones achieved on time.
Timelines updated for Phase 2.
EOF &&

# Text 2
cat > samples/text2.txt << 'EOF'
<!-- EDIT: 2024-02-01T08:00:00Z | AUTHOR: charlie | TYPE: create -->
# Technical Specification

## Overview
System requirements for Q2 deployment.

<!-- EDIT: 2024-02-01T10:00:00Z | AUTHOR: charlie | TYPE: add -->
## Hardware Requirements
- CPU: 4 cores
- RAM: 16GB
- Storage: 500GB SSD

<!-- EDIT: 2024-02-02T11:30:00Z | AUTHOR: diana | TYPE: add -->
## Software Requirements
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Python: 3.10+

<!-- EDIT: 2024-02-03T09:00:00Z | AUTHOR: charlie | TYPE: modify -->
## Hardware Requirements
- CPU: 8 cores (updated)
- RAM: 32GB (updated)
- Storage: 1TB SSD (updated)

<!-- EDIT: 2024-02-03T14:00:00Z | AUTHOR: diana | TYPE: delete -->
## Software Requirements
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Python: 3.10+
EOF &&

# Text 3
cat > samples/text3.txt << 'EOF'
<!-- EDIT: 2024-03-01T09:00:00Z | AUTHOR: eve | TYPE: create -->
# Marketing Materials
## Brand Guidelines

<!-- EDIT: 2024-03-01T11:00:00Z | AUTHOR: eve | TYPE: add | SECTION: logo -->
## Logo
Our logo is available in multiple formats.
![Company Logo](logo.png)

<!-- EDIT: 2024-03-02T10:00:00Z | AUTHOR: frank | TYPE: add | SECTION: colors -->
## Color Palette
- Primary: #0066CC
- Secondary: #FF6600
- Accent: #66CC33
EOF &&

# PDF 1, 2, 3
python3 << 'PYEOF'
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter

c = canvas.Canvas("samples/pdf1.pdf", pagesize=letter)
c.setTitle("Sample Report Q1")
c.setAuthor("alice")
c.setSubject("Quarterly financial report")
c.drawString(100, 750, "Sample Report Q1")
c.drawString(100, 730, "Author: alice")
c.drawString(100, 710, "Sample content for testing.")
c.save()

c = canvas.Canvas("samples/pdf2.pdf", pagesize=letter)
c.setTitle("Technical Manual")
c.setAuthor("bob")
c.setSubject("Technical documentation")
c.drawString(100, 750, "Technical Manual")
c.showPage()
c.drawString(100, 750, "Page 2")
c.showPage()
c.drawString(100, 750, "Page 3")
c.save()

c = canvas.Canvas("samples/pdf3.pdf", pagesize=letter)
c.setTitle("Simple Document")
c.setAuthor("charlie")
c.drawString(100, 750, "Simple PDF")
c.save()
print("3 PDF files created")
PYEOF &&

# Excel 1, 2, 3
python3 << 'PYEOF'
import openpyxl
from openpyxl import Workbook
from datetime import datetime

# Excel 1
wb = Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Sheet1"
ws['A1'] = 'Product'; ws['B1'] = 'Quantity'; ws['C1'] = 'Price'
ws['A2'] = 'Widget A'; ws['B2'] = 100; ws['C2'] = 29.99
wb.properties.author = "alice"
wb.properties.title = "Sales Data Q1"
wb.properties.created = datetime(2024, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0)
wb.properties.modified = datetime(2024, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0)
wb.save("samples/excel1.xlsx")

# Excel 2
wb = Workbook()
wb.remove(wb.active)
ws1 = wb.create_sheet("Data"); ws1['A1'] = 'Name'; ws1['B1'] = 'Value'; ws1['A2'] = 'Item1'; ws1['B2'] = 100
ws2 = wb.create_sheet("Summary"); ws2['A1'] = 'Total'; ws2['B1'] = 300
wb.properties.author = "bob"
wb.properties.title = "Monthly Report"
wb.properties.created = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 10, 0, 0)
wb.properties.modified = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 10, 0, 0)
wb.save("samples/excel2.xlsx")

# Excel 3
wb = Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Data"
ws['A1'] = 'Name'; ws['B1'] = 'Status'; ws['A2'] = 'ProjectA'; ws['B2'] = 'Complete'
wb.properties.author = "charlie"
wb.properties.title = "Project Tracker"
wb.properties.created = datetime(2024, 1, 10, 8, 0, 0)
wb.properties.modified = datetime(2024, 1, 11, 10, 30, 0)
wb.save("samples/excel3.xlsx")
print("3 Excel files created")
PYEOF &&

# Verify all files exist
echo "=== Verifying 9 sample files ==="
ls -lh samples/
echo ""
echo "SUCCESS: All 9 sample files created!"
)




ls -lh samples/
Expected: - 3 .txt files - 3 .pdf files - 3 .xlsx files

python3 extract.py samples/text1.txt --output results/text1.json
python3 extract.py samples/text2.txt --output results/text2.json
python3 extract.py samples/text3.txt --output results/text3.json

python3 extract.py samples/pdf1.pdf --output results/pdf1.json
python3 extract.py samples/pdf2.pdf --output results/pdf2.json
python3 extract.py samples/pdf3.pdf --output results/pdf3.json

python3 extract.py samples/excel1.xlsx --output results/excel1.json
python3 extract.py samples/excel2.xlsx --output results/excel2.json
python3 extract.py samples/excel3.xlsx --output results/excel3.json
Option B: Test all at once (faster)
cd /home/karthikean.juttumaha/mini-extract/prototype
for f in samples/*.txt samples/*.pdf samples/*.xlsx; do
  echo "--- $(basename $f) ---"
  python3 extract.py "$f" --format simple
  echo ""
done




Check results summary:
cd /home/karthikean.juttumaha/mini-extract/prototype
python3 << 'PYEOF'
import json, os

results = {}
for f in ["text1", "text2", "text3", "pdf1", "pdf2", "pdf3", "excel1", "excel2", "excel3"]:
    for ext in [".json"]:
        path = f"results/{f}{ext}"
        if os.path.exists(path):
            with open(path) as fh:
                data = json.load(fh)
            results[path] = {
                "nodes": data["knowledge_graph"]["total_nodes"],
                "edges": data["knowledge_graph"]["total_edges"],
                "sources": data["summary"]["sources_used"],
                "confidence": data["summary"]["confidence_distribution"]
            }

print("RESULTS SUMMARY:")
print("=" * 60)
for path, info in sorted(results.items()):
    print(f"{os.path.basename(path):20s} | Nodes: {info['nodes']:2d} | Edges: {info['edges']:2d} | Sources: {info['sources']} | Conf: {info['confidence']}")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"Total files processed: {len(results)}")
PYEOF

title: Excel File Samples (3 files)
text:
Use these commands to create the 3 Excel sample files for testing.



You can create Excel files directly with Python using openpyxl.

##File 1: excel1.xlsx - Basic workbook with metadata


cd /home/karthikean.juttumaha/mini-extract/prototype
python3 << 'ENDOFSCRIPT'
import openpyxl
from openpyxl import Workbook
from datetime import datetime

# Create workbook
wb = Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Sheet1"

# Add data
ws['A1'] = 'Product'
ws['B1'] = 'Quantity'
ws['C1'] = 'Price'
ws['A2'] = 'Widget A'
ws['B2'] = 100
ws['C2'] = 29.99
ws['A3'] = 'Widget B'
ws['B3'] = 200
ws['C3'] = 49.99

# Add metadata
wb.properties.author = "alice"
wb.properties.title = "Sales Data Q1"
wb.properties.subject = "Quarterly sales report"
wb.properties.created = datetime(2024, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0)
wb.properties.modified = datetime(2024, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0)

# Save
wb.save("samples/excel1.xlsx")
print("excel1.xlsx created successfully")
ENDOFSCRIPT




Nodes: 1 (creation) + 1 file node = 2 total
Author: alice
Title: Sales Data Q1
Sheets: Sheet1
Source: excel
Confidence: High

The extractor will extract: - Author (workbook properties) - Title (if set) - Subject (if set) - Creation Date - Modification Date - Sheet Count (number of sheets) - Sheet Names (list of all sheet names)
Output will include: - Edit nodes for creation and modification (if timestamps differ) - File node with Excel type - Knowledge graph showing file -> edit relationships - High confidence scores - Each edit node contains metadata with sheet information




Run this single command to create all 3 Excel files:
cd /home/karthikean.juttumaha/mini-extract/prototype

# Install dependency
pip install openpyxl 2>/dev/null

title: Universal File Extraction Script
text:
This is the main Python script template for the Universal File Metadata & Version History Extractor.



Copy the following code to create extract.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Universal File Metadata & Version History Extractor

Extracts maximum information from any file, tracks all historical changes,
builds knowledge graphs, and assigns confidence scores.

Usage:
    python extract.py <file_path> [--output OUTPUT_FILE]
    
Example:
    python extract.py document.txt --output result.json
"""

import os
import sys
import json
import re
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
import argparse


# ============================================================================
# DATA CLASSES
# ============================================================================

class EditNode:
    """Represents a single edit/change to a file."""
    
    def __init__(self, edit_id: str, timestamp: str, author: Optional[str],
                 edit_type: str, content_before: Optional[str] = None,
                 content_after: Optional[str] = None,
                 affected_sections: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                 description: str = "", file_version: str = "1.0",
                 source: str = "unknown", confidence: str = "medium"):
        self.edit_id = edit_id
        self.timestamp = timestamp
        self.author = author
        self.edit_type = edit_type
        self.content_before = content_before
        self.content_after = content_after
        self.affected_sections = affected_sections or []
        self.description = description
        self.file_version = file_version
        self.source = source
        self.confidence = confidence
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "node_id": self.edit_id,
            "node_type": "edit",
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "author": self.author,
            "edit_type": self.edit_type,
            "content_before": self.content_before,
            "content_after": self.content_after,
            "affected_sections": self.affected_sections,
            "description": self.description,
            "file_version": self.file_version,
            "source": self.source,
            "evaluation_band": self.confidence
        }


class KnowledgeGraph:
    """Directed graph representing file evolution."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.nodes: List[Dict] = []
        self.edges: List[Dict] = []
    
    def add_node(self, node_data: Dict) -> str:
        """Add a node to the graph."""
        node_id = node_data.get("node_id", hashlib.md5(json.dumps(node_data).encode()).hexdigest())
        node_data["node_id"] = node_id
        self.nodes.append(node_data)
        return node_id
    
    def add_edge(self, source_id: str, target_id: str, relationship: str,
                 timestamp: str, edge_type: str = "temporal", weight: float = 1.0) -> str:
        """Add an edge between nodes."""
        edge_id = f"edge_{source_id}_{target_id}"
        edge = {
            "edge_id": edge_id,
            "source": source_id,
            "target": target_id,
            "edge_type": edge_type,
            "relationship": relationship,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "weight": weight
        }
        self.edges.append(edge)
        return edge_id
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "nodes": self.nodes,
            "edges": self.edges,
            "total_nodes": len(self.nodes),
            "total_edges": len(self.edges)
        }

# ============================================================================

class VersionHistoryExtractor:
    """Extracts version history from files using multiple methods."""
    
    def extract(self, file_path: Path) -> List[EditNode]:
        """Main extraction method - tries all available sources."""
        edits = []
        
        # Try each extraction method
        for extractor in [
            self._extract_from_embedded_markers,
            self._extract_from_filesystem,
        ]:
            try:
                result = extractor(file_path)
                if result:
                    edits.extend(result)
                    # If we got results from a good source, stop
                    if edits and edits[0].source in ["embedded_marker"]:
                        break
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Warning: {extractor.__name__} failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                continue
        
        # Sort by timestamp
        edits.sort(key=lambda x: x.timestamp)
        
        # Assign sequential versions
        for i, edit in enumerate(edits):
            edit.file_version = f"{i + 1}.0"
        
        return edits
    
    def _extract_from_embedded_markers(self, file_path: Path) -> List[EditNode]:
        """Extract edit history from embedded HTML-style markers."""
        edits = []
        
        # Only process text-based files
        if not file_path.name.endswith(('.txt', '.md')):
            return edits
        
        try:
            with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                content = f.read()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Cannot read file {file_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return edits
        
        # Pattern: <!-- EDIT: 2024-02-02T20:31:00Z | AUTHOR: alice | TYPE: add | SECTION: header -->
        pattern = r'<!--\s*EDIT:\s*([^|]+)\s*\|\s*AUTHOR:\s*([^|]+)\s*\|\s*TYPE:\s*([^|]+)'
        
        for i, match in enumerate(re.finditer(pattern, content)):
            timestamp = match.group(1).strip()
            author = match.group(2).strip()
            edit_type = match.group(3).strip().lower()
            
            # Get content after this marker
            content_start = match.end()
            next_match = next((m for m in re.finditer(pattern, content[content_start:])), None)
            
            if next_match:
                content_end = content_start + next_match.start()
            else:
                content_end = len(content)
            
            content_after = content[content_start:content_end].strip()
            
            # For delete operations, the marker indicates removal
            content_before = None
            if edit_type == "delete":
                # Look for content before the marker (previous edit's content)
                prev_matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content[:content_start]))
                if prev_matches:
                    prev_match = prev_matches[-1]
                    content_before = content[prev_match.end():content_start].strip()
            
            edit_id = f"edit_{timestamp.replace(':', '').replace('-', '').replace('T', '').replace('Z', '')}_{i}"
            
            edit = EditNode(
                edit_id=edit_id,
                timestamp=timestamp,
                author=author if author.lower() != "none" else None,
                edit_type=edit_type,
                content_before=content_before,
                content_after=content_after if edit_type != "delete" else None,
                source="embedded_marker",
                confidence="high"
            )
            edits.append(edit)
        
        return edits
    
    def _extract_from_filesystem(self, file_path: Path) -> List[EditNode]:
        """Fallback: use file system metadata."""
        try:
            stat = file_path.stat()
            timestamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime).isoformat() + "Z"
            
            edit_id = f"fs_{file_path.name}"
            
            # Try to get content
            try:
                with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                    content = f.read()
            except:
                content = f"[Binary file: {file_path.name}]"
            
            edit = EditNode(
                edit_id=edit_id,
                timestamp=timestamp,
                author=None,
                edit_type="create",
                content_after=content[:500] + "..." if len(content) > 500 else content,
                source="filesystem",
                confidence="low"
            )
            return [edit]
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Filesystem extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return []


# ============================================================================
# MAIN EXTRACTION FUNCTION
# ============================================================================

def extract_file(file_path: str, git_repo_path: Optional[str] = None,
                 output_format: str = "json") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Extract all information from a file and build knowledge graph.
    
    Args:
        file_path: Path to the file
        git_repo_path: Optional git repository path
        output_format: Output format (json, graphml, gexf)
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary with extraction results
    """
    file_path = Path(file_path)
    
    if not file_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}")
    
    # Step 1: Extract metadata
    metadata = _extract_metadata(file_path)
    
    # Step 2: Extract version history
    version_extractor = VersionHistoryExtractor()
    edits = version_extractor.extract(file_path)
    
    # Step 3: Build knowledge graph
    kg = KnowledgeGraph()
    
    # Add edit nodes
    for edit in edits:
        kg.add_node(edit.to_dict())
    
    # Add edges between consecutive edits
    for i in range(len(edits) - 1):
        current = edits[i]
        next_edit = edits[i + 1]
        
        # Determine relationship
        if current.edit_type == "delete" and next_edit.edit_type == "add":
            relationship = "replaces"
        elif current.edit_type in ["create", "add"] and next_edit.edit_type in ["add", "modify"]:
            relationship = "adds_to"
        elif current.edit_type == "create":
            relationship = "adds_to"
        else:
            relationship = "modifies"
        
        kg.add_edge(
            current.edit_id,
            next_edit.edit_id,
            relationship=relationship,
            timestamp=next_edit.timestamp
        )
    
    # Step 4: Build result
    result = {
        "extraction_metadata": {
            "file": str(file_path),
            "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z",
            "extractor_version": "1.0.0"
        },
        "file_metadata": metadata,
        "version_history": {
            "edits": [e.to_dict() for e in edits],
            "edit_count": len(edits)
        },
        "knowledge_graph": kg.to_dict(),
        "summary": {
            "total_edits": len(edits),
            "total_nodes": len(kg.nodes),
            "total_edges": len(kg.edges),
            "sources_used": list(set(e.source for e in edits)),
            "confidence_distribution": {
                "high": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "high"),
                "medium": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "medium"),
                "low": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "low")
            }
        }
    }
    
    return result


def _extract_metadata(file_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Extract basic metadata from file."""
    try:
        stat = file_path.stat()
        metadata = {
            "filesystem": {
                "size_bytes": stat.st_size,
                "created_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_ctime).isoformat() + "Z",
                "modified_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime).isoformat() + "Z",
                "accessed_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_atime).isoformat() + "Z",
            }
        }
        
        # For text files, try to read content
        if file_path.name.endswith(('.txt', '.md', '.csv', '.json', '.xml', '.html', '.py', '.js')):
            try:
                with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                    content = f.read()
                metadata["text"] = {
                    "character_count": len(content),
                    "line_count": content.count('\n') + 1,
                    "word_count": len(content.split())
                }
            except:
                pass
        
        return metadata
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Metadata extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return {}


# ============================================================================
# MAIN CLI
# ============================================================================

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='Universal File Metadata & Version History Extractor',
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
    )
    
    parser.add_argument('file', help='Path to the file to extract')
    parser.add_argument('--git-repo', help='Path to git repository (optional)')
    parser.add_argument('--output-format', choices=['json', 'graphml', 'gexf'],
                        default='json', help='Output format (default: json)')
    parser.add_argument('--output', '-o', help='Output file path (default: stdout)')
    parser.add_argument('--verbose', '-v', action='store_true', help='Verbose output')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    try:
        result = extract_file(
            args.file,
            git_repo_path=args.git_repo,
            output_format=args.output_format
        )
        
        # Format output
        if args.output_format == 'json':
            output = json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)
        elif args.output_format == 'graphml':
            output = knowledge_graph_to_graphml(result.get('knowledge_graph', {}))
        elif args.output_format == 'gexf':
            output = knowledge_graph_to_gexf(result.get('knowledge_graph', {}))
        else:
            output = json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)
        
        # Write output
        if args.output:
            with open(args.output, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write(output)
            print(f"Results saved to: {args.output}", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            print(output)
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


def knowledge_graph_to_graphml(kg: Dict) -> str:
    """Convert knowledge graph to GraphML format."""
    lines = [
        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
        '<graphml xmlns="http://graphml.graphdrawing.org/xmlns"',
        '    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"',
        '    xsi:schemaLocation="http://graphml.graphdrawing.org/xmlns',
        '    http://graphml.graphdrawing.org/xmlns/1.0/graphml.xsd">',
        '  <key id="timestamp" for="node" attr.name="timestamp" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="author" for="node" attr.name="author" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="edit_type" for="node" attr.name="edit_type" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="confidence" for="node" attr.name="confidence" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="relationship" for="edge" attr.name="relationship" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="weight" for="edge" attr.name="weight" attr.type="double"/>',
        '  <graph id="FileHistory" edgemode="directed">'
    ]
    
    for node in kg.get('nodes', []):
        node_id = node.get('node_id', 'unknown')
        lines.append(f'    <node id="{node_id}">')
        if node.get('timestamp'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="timestamp">{node["timestamp"]}</data>')
        if node.get('author'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="author">{node["author"]}</data>')
        if node.get('edit_type'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="edit_type">{node["edit_type"]}</data>')
        if node.get('evaluation_band'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="confidence">{node["evaluation_band"]}</data>')
        lines.append('    </node>')
    
    for edge in kg.get('edges', []):
        lines.append(f'    <edge id="{edge.get("edge_id", "unknown")}" source="{edge.get("source", "unknown")}" target="{edge.get("target", "unknown")}">')
        if edge.get('relationship'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="relationship">{edge["relationship"]}</data>')
        lines.append(f'      <data key="weight">{edge.get("weight", 1.0)}</data>')
        lines.append('    </edge>')
    
    lines.extend(['  </graph>', '</graphml>'])
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def knowledge_graph_to_gexf(kg: Dict) -> str:
    """Convert knowledge graph to GEXF format (for Gephi)."""
    lines = [
        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
        '<gexf xmlns="http://www.gexf.net/1.2draft" version="1.2">',
        '  <meta lastmodifieddate="' + datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + '">',
        '    <creator>File History Extractor</creator>',
        '    <description>File edit history knowledge graph</description>',
        '  </meta>',
        '  <graph mode="static" defaultedgetype="directed">',
        '    <attributes class="node">',
        '      <attribute id="0" title="timestamp" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="1" title="author" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="2" title="edit_type" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="3" title="confidence" type="string"/>',
        '    </attributes>',
        '    <attributes class="edge">',
        '      <attribute id="0" title="relationship" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="1" title="weight" type="float"/>',
        '    </attributes>',
        '    <nodes>'
    ]
    
    for node in kg.get('nodes', []):
        node_id = node.get('node_id', 'unknown')
        label = node.get('description', node.get('edit_type', 'edit'))[:30]
        lines.append(f'      <node id="{node_id}" label="{label}">')
        lines.append('        <attvalues>')
        if node.get('timestamp'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="0" value="{node["timestamp"]}"/>')
        if node.get('author'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="1" value="{node["author"]}"/>')
        if node.get('edit_type'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="2" value="{node["edit_type"]}"/>')
        if node.get('evaluation_band'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="3" value="{node["evaluation_band"]}"/>')
        lines.append('        </attvalues>')
        lines.append('      </node>')
    
    lines.append('    </nodes>')
    lines.append('    <edges>')
    
    for edge in kg.get('edges', []):
        lines.append(f'      <edge id="{edge.get("edge_id", "unknown")}" source="{edge.get("source", "unknown")}" target="{edge.get("target", "unknown")}">')
        lines.append('        <attvalues>')
        if edge.get('relationship'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="0" value="{edge["relationship"]}"/>')
        lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="1" value="{edge.get("weight", 1.0)}"/>')
        lines.append('        </attvalues>')
        lines.append('      </edge>')
    
    lines.extend(['    </edges>', '  </graph>', '</gexf>'])
    return '\n'.join(lines)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

class EditNode:

                 content_after: Optional[str] = None,
                 affected_sections: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                 description: str = "", file_version: str = "1.0",
                 source: str = "unknown", confidence: str = "medium"):

        self.description = description
        self.file_version = file_version
        self.source = source
        self.confidence = confidence
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "node_id": self.edit_id,
            "node_type": "edit",
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "author": self.author,
            "edit_type": self.edit_type,
            "content_before": self.content_before,
            "content_after": self.content_after,

    # Step 4: Build result
    result = {
        "extraction_metadata": {
            "file": str(file_path),
            "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z",
            "extractor_version": "1.0.0"
        },
        "file_metadata": metadata,
        "version_history": {
            "edits": [e.to_dict() for e in edits],
            "edit_count": len(edits)
        },
        "knowledge_graph": kg.to_dict(),
        "summary": {
            "total_edits": len(edits),
            "total_nodes": len(kg.nodes),
            "total_edges": len(kg.edges),
            "sources_used": list(set(e.source for e in edits)),
            "confidence_distribution": {
                "high": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "high"),
                "medium": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "medium"),
                "low": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "low")
            }
        }
    }
    
    return result


def _extract_metadata(file_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Extract basic metadata from file."""
    try:
        stat = file_path.stat()
        metadata = {
            "filesystem": {
                "size_bytes": stat.st_size,
                "created_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_ctime).isoformat() + "Z",
                "modified_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime).isoformat() + "Z",
                "accessed_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_atime).isoformat() + "Z",
            }
        }
        
        # For text files, try to read content
        if file_path.name.endswith(('.txt', '.md', '.csv', '.json', '.xml', '.html', '.py', '.js')):
            try:
                with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                    content = f.read()
                metadata["text"] = {
                    "character_count": len(content),
                    "line_count": content.count('\n') + 1,
                    "word_count": len(content.split())
                }
            except:
                pass
        
        return metadata
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Metadata extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return {}


# ============================================================================
# MAIN CLI
# ============================================================================

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='Universal File Metadata & Version History Extractor',
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
    )
    
    parser.add_argument('file', help='Path to the file to extract')
    parser.add_argument('--git-repo', help='Path to git repository (optional)')
    parser.add_argument('--output-format', choices=['json', 'graphml', 'gexf'],
                        default='json', help='Output format (default: json)')
    parser.add_argument('--output', '-o', help='Output file path (default: stdout)')
    parser.add_argument('--verbose', '-v', action='store_true', help='Verbose output')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    try:
        result = extract_file(
            args.file,
            git_repo_path=args.git_repo,
            output_format=args.output_format
        )
        
        # Format output
        if args.output_format == 'json':
            output = json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)
        elif args.output_format == 'graphml':
            output = knowledge_graph_to_graphml(result.get('knowledge_graph', {}))
        elif args.output_format == 'gexf':
            output = knowledge_graph_to_gexf(result.get('knowledge_graph', {}))
        else:
            output = json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)
        
        # Write output
        if args.output:
            with open(args.output, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write(output)
            print(f"Results saved to: {args.output}", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            print(output)
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


def knowledge_graph_to_graphml(kg: Dict) -> str:
    """Convert knowledge graph to GraphML format."""
    lines = [
        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
        '<graphml xmlns="http://graphml.graphdrawing.org/xmlns"',
        '    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"',
        '    xsi:schemaLocation="http://graphml.graphdrawing.org/xmlns',
        '    http://graphml.graphdrawing.org/xmlns/1.0/graphml.xsd">',
        '  <key id="timestamp" for="node" attr.name="timestamp" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="author" for="node" attr.name="author" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="edit_type" for="node" attr.name="edit_type" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="confidence" for="node" attr.name="confidence" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="relationship" for="edge" attr.name="relationship" attr.type="string"/>',
        '  <key id="weight" for="edge" attr.name="weight" attr.type="double"/>',
        '  <graph id="FileHistory" edgemode="directed">'
    ]
    
    for node in kg.get('nodes', []):
        node_id = node.get('node_id', 'unknown')
        lines.append(f'    <node id="{node_id}">')
        if node.get('timestamp'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="timestamp">{node["timestamp"]}</data>')
        if node.get('author'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="author">{node["author"]}</data>')
        if node.get('edit_type'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="edit_type">{node["edit_type"]}</data>')
        if node.get('evaluation_band'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="confidence">{node["evaluation_band"]}</data>')
        lines.append('    </node>')
    
    for edge in kg.get('edges', []):
        lines.append(f'    <edge id="{edge.get("edge_id", "unknown")}" source="{edge.get("source", "unknown")}" target="{edge.get("target", "unknown")}">')
        if edge.get('relationship'):
            lines.append(f'      <data key="relationship">{edge["relationship"]}</data>')
        lines.append(f'      <data key="weight">{edge.get("weight", 1.0)}</data>')
        lines.append('    </edge>')
    
    lines.extend(['  </graph>', '</graphml>'])
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def knowledge_graph_to_gexf(kg: Dict) -> str:
    """Convert knowledge graph to GEXF format (for Gephi)."""
    lines = [
        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
        '<gexf xmlns="http://www.gexf.net/1.2draft" version="1.2">',
        '  <meta lastmodifieddate="' + datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + '">',
        '    <creator>File History Extractor</creator>',
        '    <description>File edit history knowledge graph</description>',
        '  </meta>',
        '  <graph mode="static" defaultedgetype="directed">',
        '    <attributes class="node">',
        '      <attribute id="0" title="timestamp" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="1" title="author" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="2" title="edit_type" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="3" title="confidence" type="string"/>',
        '    </attributes>',
        '    <attributes class="edge">',
        '      <attribute id="0" title="relationship" type="string"/>',
        '      <attribute id="1" title="weight" type="float"/>',
        '    </attributes>',
        '    <nodes>'
    ]
    
    for node in kg.get('nodes', []):
        node_id = node.get('node_id', 'unknown')
        label = node.get('description', node.get('edit_type', 'edit'))[:30]
        lines.append(f'      <node id="{node_id}" label="{label}">')
        lines.append('        <attvalues>')
        if node.get('timestamp'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="0" value="{node["timestamp"]}"/>')
        if node.get('author'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="1" value="{node["author"]}"/>')
        if node.get('edit_type'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="2" value="{node["edit_type"]}"/>')
        if node.get('evaluation_band'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="3" value="{node["evaluation_band"]}"/>')
        lines.append('        </attvalues>')
        lines.append('      </node>')
    
    lines.append('    </nodes>')
    lines.append('    <edges>')
    
    for edge in kg.get('edges', []):
        lines.append(f'      <edge id="{edge.get("edge_id", "unknown")}" source="{edge.get("source", "unknown")}" target="{edge.get("target", "unknown")}">')
        lines.append('        <attvalues>')
        if edge.get('relationship'):
            lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="0" value="{edge["relationship"]}"/>')
        lines.append(f'          <attvalue for="1" value="{edge.get("weight", 1.0)}"/>')
        lines.append('        </attvalues>')
        lines.append('      </edge>')
    
    lines.extend(['    </edges>', '  </graph>', '</gexf>'])
    return '\n'.join(lines)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

text:
This is the complete Python script with PDF and Excel support for the Universal File Metadata & Version History Extractor.



This version supports: - Text files with embedded markers (high confidence) - PDF files via PyPDF2/pdfplumber (medium confidence) - Excel files via openpyxl (medium confidence) - Any file via filesystem metadata (low confidence fallback)
Copy this code to create extract.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Universal File Metadata & Version History Extractor - Full Version

Extracts maximum information from any file, tracks all historical changes,
builds knowledge graphs, and assigns confidence scores.

Supports: Text, PDF, Excel, Images, and any other file type.

Usage:
    python extract.py <file_path> [--output OUTPUT_FILE]
    
Example:
    python extract.py document.pdf --output result.json
    python extract.py data.xlsx --output result.json
"""

import os
import sys
import json
import re
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any, Tuple
import argparse

# Check for optional dependencies
try:
    import PyPDF2
    HAS_PYPdf2 = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_PYPdf2 = False

try:
    import pdfplumber
    HAS_PDFPLUMBER = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_PDFPLUMBER = False

try:
    import openpyxl
    HAS_OPENPYXL = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_OPENPYXL = False

try:
    from PIL import Image
    import PIL.ExifTags
    HAS_PIL = True
except ImportError:
    HAS_PIL = False


# ============================================================================
# DATA CLASSES
# ============================================================================

class EditNode:
    """Represents a single edit/change to a file."""
    
    def __init__(self, edit_id: str, timestamp: str, author: Optional[str] = None,
                 edit_type: str = "create", content_before: Optional[str] = None,
                 content_after: Optional[str] = None,
                 affected_sections: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                 description: str = "", file_version: str = "1.0",
                 source: str = "unknown", confidence: str = "medium",
                 metadata: Optional[Dict] = None):
        self.edit_id = edit_id
        self.timestamp = timestamp
        self.author = author
        self.edit_type = edit_type
        self.content_before = content_before
        self.content_after = content_after
        self.affected_sections = affected_sections or []
        self.description = description
        self.file_version = file_version
        self.source = source
        self.confidence = confidence
        self.metadata = metadata or {}
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        result = {
            "node_id": self.edit_id,
            "node_type": "edit",
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "author": self.author,
            "edit_type": self.edit_type,
            "content_before": self.content_before,
            "content_after": self.content_after,
            "affected_sections": self.affected_sections,
            "description": self.description,
            "file_version": self.file_version,
            "source": self.source,
            "evaluation_band": self.confidence
        }
        if self.metadata:
            result["metadata"] = self.metadata
        return result


class KnowledgeGraph:
    """Directed graph representing file evolution."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.nodes: List[Dict] = []
        self.edges: List[Dict] = []
    
    def add_node(self, node_data: Dict) -> str:
        """Add a node to the graph."""
        node_id = node_data.get("node_id")
        if not node_id:
            node_id = hashlib.md5(json.dumps(node_data).encode()).hexdigest()
            node_data["node_id"] = node_id
        self.nodes.append(node_data)
        return node_id
    
    def add_edge(self, source_id: str, target_id: str, relationship: str,
                 timestamp: str, edge_type: str = "temporal", weight: float = 1.0) -> str:
        """Add an edge between nodes."""
        edge_id = f"edge_{source_id}_{target_id}"
        edge = {
            "edge_id": edge_id,
            "source": source_id,
            "target": target_id,
            "edge_type": edge_type,
            "relationship": relationship,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "weight": weight
        }
        self.edges.append(edge)
        return edge_id
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "nodes": self.nodes,
            "edges": self.edges,
            "total_nodes": len(self.nodes),
            "total_edges": len(self.edges)
        }


# ============================================================================
# VERSION HISTORY EXTRACTOR
# ============================================================================

class VersionHistoryExtractor:
    """Extracts version history from files using multiple methods."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.extractors = [
            self._extract_from_embedded_markers,
            self._extract_from_pdf_timestamps,
            self._extract_from_excel_metadata,
            self._extract_from_filesystem,
        ]
    
    def extract(self, file_path: Path) -> Tuple[List[EditNode], str]:
        """
        Main extraction method - tries all available sources.
        
        Returns:
            Tuple of (list of EditNodes, extraction source)
        """
        all_edits = []
        sources_used = []
        
        for extractor in self.extractors:
            try:
                result, source = extractor(file_path)
                if result:
                    all_edits.extend(result)
                    sources_used.append(source)
                    # If we got results from a good source, stop
                    if source in ["embedded_marker", "pdf_plumber", "pdf_pypdf2", "excel"]:
                        break
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Warning: {extractor.__name__} failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                continue
        
        # Sort by timestamp
        all_edits.sort(key=lambda x: x.timestamp)
        
        # Assign sequential versions
        for i, edit in enumerate(all_edits):
            edit.file_version = f"{i + 1}.0"
        
        return all_edits, sources_used
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # TEXT FILE EXTRACTORS
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    def _extract_from_embedded_markers(self, file_path: Path) -> Tuple[List[EditNode], str]:
        """Extract edit history from embedded HTML-style markers."""
        edits = []
        
        # Only process text-based files
        text_extensions = ('.txt', '.md', '.csv', '.json', '.xml', '.html', '.py', '.js', '.sh')
        if not file_path.name.endswith(text_extensions):
            return edits, ""
        
        try:
            with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                content = f.read()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Cannot read file {file_path}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return edits, ""
        
        # Pattern: <!-- EDIT: 2024-02-02T20:31:00Z | AUTHOR: alice | TYPE: add -->
        pattern = r'<!--\s*EDIT:\s*([^|]+)\s*\|\s*AUTHOR:\s*([^|]+)\s*\|\s*TYPE:\s*([^|]+)'
        
        for i, match in enumerate(re.finditer(pattern, content)):
            timestamp = match.group(1).strip()
            author = match.group(2).strip()
            edit_type = match.group(3).strip().lower()
            
            # Get content after this marker
            content_start = match.end()
            content_text = content[content_start:].strip()
            
            # Find next marker or end of file
            next_match = next((m for m in re.finditer(pattern, content[content_start:])), None)
            if next_match:
                content_end = content_start + next_match.start()
                content_text = content[content_start:content_end].strip()
            
            # For delete operations, try to get content before
            content_before = None
            if edit_type == "delete":
                prev_matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content[:content_start]))
                if prev_matches:
                    prev_match = prev_matches[-1]
                    content_before = content[prev_match.end():content_start].strip()
            
            edit_id = f"edit_{hashlib.md5(timestamp.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}_{i}"
            
            edit = EditNode(
                edit_id=edit_id,
                timestamp=timestamp,
                author=author if author.lower() != "none" else None,
                edit_type=edit_type,
                content_before=content_before,
                content_after=content_text if edit_type != "delete" else None,
                source="embedded_marker",
                confidence="high"
            )
            edits.append(edit)
        
        return edits, "embedded_marker"
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # PDF FILE EXTRACTORS
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    def _extract_pdf_metadata_with_pypdf2(self, file_path: Path) -> Dict:
        """Extract metadata from PDF using PyPDF2."""
        metadata = {}
        try:
            with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
                reader = PyPDF2.PdfReader(f)
                doc_info = reader.metadata
                
                if doc_info:
                    metadata = {
                        "title": doc_info.get("/Title", ""),
                        "author": doc_info.get("/Author", ""),
                        "creator": doc_info.get("/Creator", ""),
                        "producer": doc_info.get("/Producer", ""),
                        "subject": doc_info.get("/Subject", ""),
                        "creation_date": doc_info.get("/CreationDate", ""),
                        "modification_date": doc_info.get("/ModDate", ""),
                        "page_count": len(reader.pages),
                        "source": "pypdf2"
                    }
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"PyPDF2 extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        
        return metadata
    
    def _extract_pdf_metadata_with_pdfplumber(self, file_path: Path) -> Dict:
        """Extract metadata from PDF using pdfplumber."""
        metadata = {}
        try:
            with pdfplumber.open(file_path) as pdf:
                metadata = {
                    "author": pdf.metadata.get("author", ""),
                    "title": pdf.metadata.get("title", ""),
                    "subject": pdf.metadata.get("subject", ""),
                    "creator": pdf.metadata.get("creator", ""),
                    "producer": pdf.metadata.get("producer", ""),
                    "creation_date": pdf.metadata.get("creationdate", ""),
                    "page_count": len(pdf.pages),
                    "source": "pdfplumber"
                }
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"pdfplumber extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        
        return metadata
    
    def _extract_from_pdf_timestamps(self, file_path: Path) -> Tuple[List[EditNode], str]:
        """Extract metadata from PDF files."""
        if not file_path.name.lower().endswith(('.pdf',)):
            return [], ""
        
        if not (HAS_PYPdf2 or HAS_PDFPLUMBER):
            print("Warning: Neither PyPDF2 nor pdfplumber installed. Install with: pip install PyPDF2 pdfplumber", file=sys.stderr)
            return [], ""
        
        # Try both libraries
        metadata = {}
        if HAS_PYPdf2:
            metadata = self._extract_pdf_metadata_with_pypdf2(file_path)
        if not metadata and HAS_PDFPLUMBER:
            metadata = self._extract_pdf_metadata_with_pdfplumber(file_path)
        
        if not metadata:
            return [], ""
        
        # Convert PDF dates to ISO format
        creation_date = metadata.get("creation_date", "")
        mod_date = metadata.get("modification_date", "")
        
        # PDF dates are in format: D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSZ or D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSS+00'00'
        def parse_pdf_date(pdf_date: str) -> str:
            if not pdf_date or pdf_date == "":
                return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() + "Z"
            # Remove D: prefix
            pdf_date = pdf_date.lstrip("D:")
            try:
                dt = datetime.strptime(pdf_date[:14], "%Y%m%d%H%M%S")
                return dt.isoformat() + "Z"
            except:
                return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() + "Z"
        
        # Create edit nodes
        edits = []
        
        # Creation edit
        creation_ts = parse_pdf_date(creation_date)
        edit_id = f"pdf_create_{hashlib.md5(str(file_path).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}"
        
        creation_edit = EditNode(
            edit_id=edit_id,
            timestamp=creation_ts,
            author=metadata.get("author"),
            edit_type="create",
            description=f"PDF created: {metadata.get('title', file_path.name)}",
            metadata={
                "title": metadata.get("title", ""),
                "author": metadata.get("author", ""),
                "page_count": metadata.get("page_count", 0),
                "creator": metadata.get("creator", "")
            },
            source=metadata.get("source", "pdf_metadata"),
            confidence="high"
        )
        edits.append(creation_edit)
        
        # Modification edit (if different from creation)
        mod_ts = parse_pdf_date(mod_date)
        if mod_ts != creation_ts:
            edit_id = f"pdf_modify_{hashlib.md5(str(file_path).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}"
            mod_edit = EditNode(
                edit_id=edit_id,
                timestamp=mod_ts,
                author=metadata.get("author"),
                edit_type="modify",
                description=f"PDF modified: {metadata.get('title', file_path.name)}",
                metadata={
                    "title": metadata.get("title", ""),
                    "page_count": metadata.get("page_count", 0)
                },
                source=metadata.get("source", "pdf_metadata"),
                confidence="high"
            )
            edits.append(mod_edit)
        
        return edits, metadata.get("source", "pdf_metadata")
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # EXCEL FILE EXTRACTORS
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    def _extract_from_excel_metadata(self, file_path: Path) -> Tuple[List[EditNode], str]:
        """Extract metadata from Excel files using openpyxl."""
        if not file_path.name.lower().endswith(('.xlsx', '.xls')):
            return [], ""
        
        if not HAS_OPENPYXL:
            print("Warning: openpyxl not installed. Install with: pip install openpyxl", file=sys.stderr)
            return [], ""
        
        try:
            workbook = openpyxl.load_workbook(file_path, read_only=True)
            metadata = {
                "authorized": workbook.properties.author,
                "title": workbook.properties.title,
                "subject": workbook.properties.subject,
                "category": workbook.properties.category,
                "company": workbook.properties.company,
                "created": workbook.properties.created,
                "modified": workbook.properties.modified,
                "sheet_count": len(workbook.sheetnames),
                "sheet_names": list(workbook.sheetnames)
            }
            
            # Convert dates to ISO format
            created_iso = metadata["created"].isoformat() + "Z" if metadata["created"] else ""
            modified_iso = metadata["modified"].isoformat() + "Z" if metadata["modified"] else ""
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Excel extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return [], ""
        
        edits = []
        
        # Creation edit
        if created_iso:
            edit_id = f"excel_create_{hashlib.md5(str(file_path).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}"
            creation_edit = EditNode(
                edit_id=edit_id,
                timestamp=created_iso,
                author=metadata.get("authorized"),
                edit_type="create",
                description=f"Excel workbook created: {metadata.get('title', file_path.name)}",
                metadata={
                    "title": metadata.get("title", ""),
                    "author": metadata.get("authorized", ""),
                    "sheet_count": metadata.get("sheet_count", 0),
                    "sheet_names": metadata.get("sheet_names", []),
                    "subject": metadata.get("subject", ""),
                    "category": metadata.get("category", ""),
                    "company": metadata.get("company", "")
                },
                source="excel",
                confidence="high"
            )
            edits.append(creation_edit)
        
        # Modification edit
        if modified_iso and modified_iso != created_iso:
            edit_id = f"excel_modify_{hashlib.md5(str(file_path).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}"
            mod_edit = EditNode(
                edit_id=edit_id,
                timestamp=modified_iso,
                author=metadata.get("authorized"),
                edit_type="modify",
                description=f"Excel workbook modified: {metadata.get('title', file_path.name)}",
                metadata={
                    "sheet_count": metadata.get("sheet_count", 0),
                    "sheet_names": metadata.get("sheet_names", []),
                    "title": metadata.get("title", "")
                },
                source="excel",
                confidence="high"
            )
            edits.append(mod_edit)
        
        return edits, "excel"
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # FALLBACK EXTRACTORS
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    def _extract_from_filesystem(self, file_path: Path) -> Tuple[List[EditNode], str]:
        """Fallback: use file system metadata."""
        try:
            stat = file_path.stat()
            timestamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat()
            
            edit_id = f"fs_{file_path.name}_{stat.st_mtime}"
            
            # Try to get content
            content = None
            try:
                with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                    contentLucy = f.read()
                content = contentLucy[:500] + "..." if len(contentLucy) > 500 else contentLucy
            except:
                content = f"[Binary file: {file_path.name}, size: {stat.st_size} bytes]"
            
            edit = EditNode(
                edit_id=edit_id,
                timestamp=timestamp,
                author=None,
                edit_type="create",
                content_after=content,
                metadata={
                    "file_size": stat.st_size,
                    "created_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_ctime, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                    "accessed_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_atime, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat()
                },
                source="filesystem",
                confidence="low"
            )
            return [edit], "filesystem"
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Filesystem extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return [], ""


# ============================================================================
# MAIN EXTRACTION FUNCTION
# ============================================================================

def extract_file(file_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Extract all information from a file and build knowledge graph.
    
    Args:
        file_path: Path to the file
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary with extraction results
    """
    file_path = Path(file_path)
    
    if not file_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}")
    
    # Step 1: Extract version history
    version_extractor = VersionHistoryExtractor()
    edits, sources_used = version_extractor.extract(file_path)
    
    # Step 2: Extract additional metadata
    additional_metadata = _extract_additional_metadata(file_path, edits)
    
    # Step 3: Build knowledge graph
    kg = KnowledgeGraph()
    
    # Add metadata node
    file_node = {
        "node_id": f"file_{hashlib.md5(str(file_path).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}",
        "node_type": "file",
        "name": file_path.name,
        "path": str(file_path),
        "size": file_path.stat().st_size,
        "type": _get_file_type(file_path),
        "evaluation_band": "high"
    }
    kg.add_node(file_node)
    
    # Add edit nodes
    for i, edit in enumerate(edits):
        node_dict = edit.to_dict()
        kg.add_node(node_dict)
        # Add edge from file to first edit
        if i == 0:
            kg.add_edge(file_node["node_id"], edit.edit_id, "has_edit", edit.timestamp)
    
    # Add edges between consecutive edits
    for i in range(len(edits) - 1):
        current = edits[i]
        next_edit = edits[i + 1]
        
        # Determine relationship
        if current.edit_type == "delete" and next_edit.edit_type in ["add", "create"]:
            relationship = "replaces"
        elif current.edit_type in ["create", "add"] and next_edit.edit_type in ["add", "modify"]:
            relationship = "adds_to"
        elif current.edit_type == "create":
            relationship = "adds_to"
        else:
            relationship = "modifies"
        
        kg.add_edge(
            current.edit_id,
            next_edit.edit_id,
            relationship=relationship,
            timestamp=next_edit.timestamp
        )
    
    # Step 4: Build result
    all_sources = list(set(sources_used + [e.source for e in edits]))
    
    confidence_dist = {
        "high": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "high"),
        "medium": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "medium"),
        "low": sum(1 for e in edits if e.confidence == "low")
    }
    
    result = {
        "extraction_metadata": {
            "file": str(file_path),
            "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "extractor_version": "2.0.0",
            "dependencies": {
                "PyPDF2": HAS_PYPdf2,
                "pdfplumber": HAS_PDFPLUMBER,
                "openpyxl": HAS_OPENPYXL,
                "PIL": HAS_PIL
            }
        },
        "file_metadata": additional_metadata,
        "version_history": {
            "edits": [e.to_dict() for e in edits],
            "edit_count": len(edits),
            "sources_used": all_sources
        },
        "knowledge_graph": kg.to_dict(),
        "summary": {
            "total_edits": len(edits),
            "total_nodes": len(kg.nodes) - 1,  # Exclude file node
            "total_edges": len(kg.edges),
            "sources_used": all_sources,
            "confidence_distribution": confidence_dist
        }
    }
    
    return result


def _extract_additional_metadata(file_path: Path, edits: List[EditNode]) -> Dict:
    """Extract additional metadata based on file type."""
    metadata = {"filesystem": {}}
    
    try:
        stat = file_path.stat()
        metadata["filesystem"] = {
            "size_bytes": stat.st_size,
            "created_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_ctime, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "modified_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "accessed_time": datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_atime, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat()
        }
    except:
        pass
    
    # JSON detection
    if file_path.name.endswith('.json'):
        try:
            with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
                json_data = json.load(f)
                metadata["json_content"] = {
                    "key_count": len(json_data) if isinstance(json_data, dict) else None,
                    "array_length": len(json_data) if isinstance(json_data, list) else None
                }
        except:
            pass
    
    # Text file statistics
    text_extensions = ('.txt', '.md', '.csv', '.json', '.xml', '.html', '.py', '.js', '.sh')
    if file_path.name.endswith(text_extensions):
        try:
            with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                content = f.read()
            metadata["text"] = {
                "character_count": len(content),
                "line_count": content.count('\n') + 1,
                "word_count": len(content.split())
            }
        except:
            pass
    
    # Excel metadata
    if file_path.name.lower().endswith(('.xlsx', '.xls')):
        try:
            if HAS_OPENPYXL:
                workbook = openpyxl.load_workbook(file_path, read_only=True)
                metadata["excel"] = {
                    "sheet_count": len(workbook.sheetnames),
                    "sheet_names": list(workbook.sheetnames),
                    "total_cells": sum(
                        len(list(sheet.rows)) * len(list(sheet.columns))
                        for sheet in workbook
                    )
                }
        except:
            pass
    
    # PDF metadata
    if file_path.name.lower().endswith('.pdf'):
        try:
            if HAS_PYPdf2:
                with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
                    reader = PyPDF2.PdfReader(f)
                    metadata["pdf"] = {
                        "page_count": len(reader.pages),
                        "is_encrypted": reader.is_encrypted,
                        "metadata": dict(reader.metadata) if reader.metadata else {}
                    }
            elif HAS_PDFPLUMBER:
                with pdfplumber.open(file_path) as pdf:
                    metadata["pdf"] = {
                        "page_count": len(pdf.pages),
                        "metadata": pdf.metadata
                    }
        except:
            pass
    
    return metadata


def _get_file_type(file_path: Path) -> str:
    """Get file type category."""
    ext = file_path.name.lower()
    
    if ext.endswith('.pdf'):
        return "pdf"
    elif ext.endswith(('.xlsx', '.xls')):
        return "excel"
    elif ext.endswith(('.txt', '.md', '.csv', '.tsv', '.json', '.xml', '.yaml', '.yml', '.html', '.css', '.js', '.py')):
        return "text"
    elif ext.endswith(('.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.gif', '.bmp', '.tiff', '.webp')):
        return "image"
    elif ext.endswith(('.mp3', '.wav', '.ogg', '.flac', '.aac')):
        return "audio"
    elif ext.endswith(('.mp4', '.mov', '.avi', '.mkv', '.webm', '.wmv')):
        return "video"
    elif ext.endswith('.docx'):
        return "word"
    elif ext.endswith('.zip'):
        return "archive"
    else:
        return "other"


# ============================================================================
# OUTPUT FORMATTERS
# ============================================================================

def format_json(result: Dict, pretty: bool = True) -> str:
    """Format as JSON."""
    if pretty:
        return json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)
    return json.dumps(result, default=str)


def format_simple(result: Dict) -> str:
    """Format as simple text summary."""
    lines = []
    lines.append("=" * 60)
    lines.append(f"File: {result['extraction_metadata']['file']}")
    lines.append("=" * 60)
    lines.append(f"\nVersion History:")
    lines.append(f"  Total edits: {result['summary']['total_edits']}")
    lines.append(f"  Sources: {', '.join(result['summary']['sources_used'])}")
    lines.append(f"\nKnowledge Graph:")
    lines.append(f"  Nodes: {result['summary']['total_nodes']}")
    lines.append(f"  Edges: {result['summary']['total_edges']}")
    lines.append(f"\nConfidence Distribution:")
    for band, count in result['summary']['confidence_distribution'].items():
        lines.append(f"  {band.capitalize()}: {count}")
    
    if result['version_history']['edits']:
        lines.append(f"\nEdit Timeline:")
        for edit in result['version_history']['edits']:
            lines.append(f"  [{edit['timestamp']}] {edit['author'] or 'Unknown'} - {edit['edit_type']}")
    
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ============================================================================
# MAIN CLI
# ============================================================================

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description='Universal File Metadata & Version History Extractor - Full Version',
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="""
Examples:
  python extract.py document.txt --output result.json
  python extract.py report.pdf --output result.json
  python extract.py data.xlsx --output result.json
  python extract.py image.png --simple
        """
    )
    
    parser.add_argument('file', help='Path to the file to extract')
    parser.add_argument('--output', '-o', help='Output file path (default: stdout)')
    parser.add_argument('--format', '-f', choices=['json', 'simple'],
                        default='json', help='Output format (default: json)')
    parser.add_argument('--pretty', action='store_true', default=True,
                        help='Pretty print JSON (default: True)')
    parser.add_argument('--no-pretty', action='store_false', dest='pretty')
    parser.add_argument('--verbose', '-v', action='store_true', help='Verbose output')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    # Check dependencies
    if args.verbose:
        print("Dependency Status:", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"  PyPDF2: {HAS_PYPdf2}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"  pdfplumber: {HAS_PDFPLUMBER}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"  openpyxl: {HAS_OPENPYXL}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"  PIL: {HAS_PIL}", file=sys.stderr)
    
    try:
        result = extract_file(args.file)
        
        # Format output
        if args.format == 'json':
            output = format_json(result, pretty=args.pretty)
        else:
            output = format_simple(result)
        
        # Write output
        if args.output:
            with open(args.output, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write(output)
            print(f"Output written to: {args.output}", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            print(output)
        
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Check that the file path is correct.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Extraction failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        if args.verbose:
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

This version supports: - Text files with embedded markers (high confidence) - PDF files via PyPDF2/pdfplumber (medium confidence) - Excel files via openpyxl (medium confidence) - Any file via filesystem metadata (low confidence fallback)
